name: Dynamo Release v0.4.0
body:
# Dynamo 0.4.0 Release Notes

Dynamo is a high-performance, low-latency inference framework designed to serve generative AI models—across any framework, architecture, or deployment scale. It's an open-source project under the Apache 2.0 license. Dynamo is available for installation via pip wheels and containers from NVIDIA NGC.

As a vendor-neutral serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple large language model (LLM) inference engines to varying degrees:

- **NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM**
- **vLLM**
- **SGLang**

---

## Major Features and Improvements

### Increasing Framework Support

- **vLLM Updates**  
  - Added E2E integration tests ([#1935](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1935)) and multimodal example with Llama4 Maverick ([#1990](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1990))  
  - Prefill-aware routing for improved performance ([#1895](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1895))  
  - Configurable namespace support for vLLM examples ([#1909](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1909))  
  - Routing via `ApproxKvIndexer` with `use_kv_events` flag ([#1869](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1869))
  - Updated all vLLM examples to new UX ([#1756](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1756))

- **SGLang Updates**  
  - Receive KV metrics from scheduler ([#1789](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1789))  
  - Disaggregated deployment examples ([#2137](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2137))  
  - Launch and deploy examples added ([#2068](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2068))

- **TRT-LLM Updates**  
  - New/speculative decoding example: Llama-4 + Eagle-3 ([#1828](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1828))

- **Routing Performance**  
  - Removed router hot-path lock for faster request handling ([#1963](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1963))  
  - Added radix tree dumps as router events ([#2057](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2057))
  
---

### UX Updates

- **Migration to New Python UX**
  - Updated all Python launch flows to the new UX structure ([#2003](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2003)), including refactoring vLLM backend integration ([#1983](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1983)).
  - Removed outdated examples that relied on the old UX ([#1899](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1899)).

- **CLI and Packaging Enhancements**
  - Added Python bindings for Dynamo CLI tools ([#1799](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1799)).
  - Updated Python packaging to align with the new UX ([#2054](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2054)).
  - Introduced a Python frontend/ingress node for easier deployment integration ([#1912](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1912)).
  - Added a convenience script to uninstall Dynamo Deploy CRDs ([#1933](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1933)).

- **Kubernetes Deployment UX**
  - Enhanced Helm chart flexibility:  
    - Added ability to override any `podSpec` property ([#2116](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2116)).  
    - Enabled Helm upgrade via `deploy` script for smoother iteration ([#1936](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1936)).  
    - Added Grove scheduling support to the graph Helm chart ([#1954](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1954)).
  - Introduced Kubernetes deployment examples for vLLM, SGLang, and TRT-LLM ([#2062](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2062), [#2133](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2133)).
  - New Hello World Kubernetes deployment example ([#1854](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1854)).

- **Examples & Docs Overhaul**
  - Hello World Python binding example ([#2083](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2083)).
  - Documentation updated for UX ([#2070](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2070)), reorganized example READMEs ([#2174](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2174)), and refactored core README structure ([#2141](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2141)).

---

### Deployment, Kubernetes, and CLI

- **Helm and Graph Deployments**  
  - Liveness/readiness probes in graph Helm chart ([#1888](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1888))  
  - Added ability to override any `podSpec` property ([#2116](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2116))  
  - Support for Grove scheduling in Helm ([#1954](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1954))

- **Planner and Profiling**  
  - Deploy SLA profiler and SLA planner to Kubernetes ([#2030](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2030), [#2135](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2135))

---

### Performance and Observability

- **Structured Logging Improvements**  
  - Enhanced structured JSONL logs with span start/close events, trace ID/span ID injection, duration formatting in microseconds, and improved context capture for distributed tracing workflows (PR [#2061](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2061)).

- **Tokenizer & Runtime**  
  - De-tokenize performance improved by ~50% ([#1868](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1868))  
  - Runtime now uses all available parallelism ([#1858](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1858))

- **Metrics**  
  - Hierarchical Prometheus metrics registry ([#2008](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2008))  
  - Generic ingress handler metrics ([#2090](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2090))

---

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed GPU resource specifications in LLM deployments ([#1812](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1812))  
- Corrected vLLM, SGLang, and TRTLLM deployment issues, including container builds, runtime packaging, and helm chart updates ([#1942](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1942), [#2062](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2062), [#1825](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1825))  
- Addressed port conflicts, deterministic port assignments, and health check improvements ([#1937](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1937), [#1996](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1996))  
- Improved error handling for empty message lists and invalid configurations ([#2067](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2067), [#2071](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2071))  
- Fixed nil pointer dereference issues in the Dynamo controller ([#2299](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2299), [#2335](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2335))  
- Locked dependencies to avoid breaking changes (e.g., Triton 3.4.0 w/ TRT-LLM 1.0.0) ([#2233](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/2233))

---

## Documentation

- **Guides and Examples**

name: Dynamo Release v0.3.2
body:
Dynamo  is a high-performance, low-latency inference framework designed to serve generative AI models—across any framework, architecture, or deployment scale. It's an open source project under the Apache 2.0 license. Dynamo is available for installation via pip wheels and containers from NVIDIA NGC.

As a vendor-neutral serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple large language model (LLM) inference engines to varying degrees:

- NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
- vLLM
- SGLang

## Major Features and Improvements

### Engine Support and Routing

- Example standalone router for use outside of dynamo ([#1409](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1409)).
- The new SLA-based planner dynamically manages resource allocation based on service-level objectives ([#1420](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1420)).
- Data-parallel vLLM worker setups are now supported ([#1513](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1513)).
- SGLang support was extended for DeepEP deployments ([#1120](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1120)).
- Clean shutdown is now available for vllm_v1 and SGLang engines ([#1562](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1562), [#1764](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1764)).
- Experimental support for WideEP with EPLB aggregation and disaggregation is now available for TRTLLM ([#1652](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1652), [#1690](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1690)).
- Approximate KV cache residency and predicted active KV blocks for improved routing efficiency ([#1636](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1636), [#1638](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1638), [#1731](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1731)).

### Observability and Metrics

- Native DCGM and Prometheus integration enables hardware metrics collection and export. Optional Grafana dashboards are provided ([#1488](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1488), [#1701](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1701), [#1788](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1788)).
- New Grafana dashboards offer composite software and hardware system visibility ([#1788](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1788)).
- Batch `/completions` endpoint and speculative decoding metrics are now supported for vLLM ([#1626](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1626), [#1549](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1549)).

### Deployment, Kubernetes, and CLI

- The Kubernetes operator now supports custom entrypoints, command overrides, and simplified graph deployments ([#1396](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1396), [#1708](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1708), [#1877](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1877), [#1893](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1893)).
- Example manifests for multimodal and minimal deployments were added ([#1836](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1836), [#1872](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1872)).
- Graph Helm chart logic, resource requests, and health probes were improved ([#1877](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1877), [#1888](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1893)).
- Two new Helm charts are introduced in this release: dynamo-platform, and dynamo-crds, enabling modular and robust Kubernetes deployments for a variety of topologies and operational requirements.
- The `dynamo-run` command line interface now supports the `--version` flag and improved error handling and validation ([#1596](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1596), [#1674](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1674), [#1623](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1623)).
- Docker and Kubernetes deployment workflows were streamlined. Helm charts and container images were improved ([#1742](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1742), [#1796](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1796), [#1840](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1840), [#1841](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1841)).

### Developer Experience

- Embedding request handling was improved with frontend tokenization ([#1494](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1494)).
- OpenAI API request validation is now available ([#1674](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1674)).
- Batch embedding and parallel tokenization improve efficiency for batch inference and embedding ([#1657](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1657)).
- The `/responses` endpoint and additional API features were added ([#1694](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1694)).

## Bug Fixes

- Issues related to GPU resource specifications in deployments, container builds, and runtime were fixed ([#1826](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1826), [#1792](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1792), [#1546](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1546)).
- Helm chart logic, resource requests, and health probes were corrected ([#1877](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1877), [#1893](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1893)).
- Error handling and model loading were improved for multimodal and distributed deployments ([#1545](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1545)).
- Metrics publishing and logging were fixed for vLLM, SGLang, and OpenAI endpoints ([#1864](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1864), [#1649](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1649), [#1639](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1639)).
- Process cleanup issues were resolved in tests ([#1801](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1801)).

## Documentation

- Documentation updates include new guides for Ray setup, architecture diagrams, and deployment modes ([#1947](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1947), [#1697](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1697)).
- Benchmarking, troubleshooting, and advanced usage scenario documentation was enhanced.
- Notes were added to deprecate outdated connectors ([#1964](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1964), [#1959](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1959)).

## Build, CI, and Test

- Dependency upgrades include protobuf, nats, and etcd ([#1876](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1876), [#1744](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1744)).
- CI coverage now includes GPU-based and multi-engine tests.
- Container builds now use distroless images for improved security and efficiency ([#1570](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1570), [#1569](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1569)).
- Fault tolerance tests [#1444](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/1444)

## Known Issues

- KVBM is supported only with Python 3.12.

## Release Assets

**Python Wheels:**
- [ai-dynamo v0.3.2](https://pypi.org/project/ai-dynamo/0.3.2/)
- [ai-dynamo-runtime v0.3.2](https://pypi.org/project/ai-dynamo-runtime/0.3.2/)
- [ai-dynamo-vllm v0.8.4.post4](https://pypi.org/project/ai-dynamo-vllm/0.8.4.post4/)

**Rust Crates:**
- [dynamo-runtime v0.3.2](https://crates.io/crates/dynamo-runtime/0.3.2)
- [dynamo-llm v0.3.2](https://crates.io/crates/dynamo-llm/0.3.2)

**Containers:**
- [nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/containers/vllm-runtime/tags)
- [nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/tensorrtllm-runtime:0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/containers/tensorrtllm-runtime/tags)
- [nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/sglang-runtime:0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/containers/sglang-runtime/tags)
- [nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/kubernetes-operator:0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/containers/kubernetes-operator/tags)

**Helm Charts:**
- [dynamo-crds-0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/helm-charts/dynamo-crds)
- [dynamo-platform-0.3.2](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/ai-dynamo/helm-charts/dynamo-platform)

## Contributors

Thank you to all contributors for this release. For a full list, refer to the [changelog](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2).

name: Dynamo Release v0.3.1
body:
Dynamo is an open source project under the Apache 2.0 license. The primary distribution is done through pip wheels with minimal binary size. The ai-dynamo GitHub organization hosts two repositories: Dynamo and NIXL. Dynamo is designed as the next-generation inference server, building upon the foundation of NVIDIA® Triton Inference Server™. While Triton focuses on single-node inference deployments, we're integrating its robust capabilities into Dynamo over the next several months. We'll maintain support for Triton while providing a clear migration path for existing users once Dynamo achieves feature parity.

As a vendor-neutral serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple large language model (LLM) inference engines to varying degrees:
* NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
* vLLM
* SGLang

Dynamo v0.3.1 features:
* Functional DeepSeek R1 disaggregated serving with wide EP using SGLang
* Functional EPD disaggregation with video model (Llava video 7B) 
* Proof of concept inference gateway support 
* Prebuilt Dynamo + vLLM container 
  * We plan to release these pre-built containers in the coming days
* Amazon Linux support


Future plans
[Dynamo Roadmap](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/762)

Known Issues
* KVBM is supported only with python 3.12

name: Dynamo Release v0.3.0
body:
Dynamo is an open source project under the Apache 2.0 license. The primary distribution is done through pip wheels with minimal binary size. The ai-dynamo GitHub organization hosts two repositories: Dynamo and NIXL. Dynamo is designed as the next-generation inference server, building upon the foundation of NVIDIA® Triton Inference Server™. While Triton focuses on single-node inference deployments, we're integrating its robust capabilities into Dynamo over the next several months. We'll maintain support for Triton while providing a clear migration path for existing users once Dynamo achieves feature parity.

As a vendor-neutral serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple large language model (LLM) inference engines to varying degrees:
* NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
* vLLM
* SGLang

Dynamo v0.3.0 features:
* Dynamo run with KV routing and multiple model support! [guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/release/0.3.0/docs/guides/dynamo_run.md)
* Vllm v1 engine support! [example](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/release/0.3.0/examples/vllm_v1)
* Sglang with DP attention! [example](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/release/0.3.0/examples/sglang)
* SLA based planner! [guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/release/0.3.0/docs/guides/planner.md)
* Optimized embedding transfer for multi-modal! [example](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/release/0.3.0/examples/multimodal)
* Dynamo deploy update command! [guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/guides/dynamo_deploy/operator_deployment.md#managing-deployments)
* Model caching using Fluid! [guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/guides/dynamo_deploy/model_caching_with_fluid.md)
* Fluxcd guide to managing custom resources [guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/guides/dynamo_deploy/dynamo_operator.md#gitops-deployment-with-fluxcd)

Future plans
[Dynamo Roadmap](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/762)

Known Issues
* KVBM is supported only with python 3.12

name: Dynamo Release v0.2.0
body:
Dynamo is an open source project with Apache 2 license. The primary distribution is done via pip wheels with minimal binary size. The ai-dynamo github org hosts 2 repos: dynamo and NIXL. Dynamo is designed as the ideal next generation inference server, building upon the foundations of the Triton Inference Server. While Triton focuses on single-node inference deployments, we are committed to integrating its robust single-node capabilities into Dynamo within the next several months. We will maintain ongoing support for Triton while ensuring a seamless migration path for existing users to Dynamo once feature parity is achieved. As a vendor-agnostic serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple LLM inference engines including TRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang, with varying degrees of maturity and support. 

**Dynamo v0.2.0 features:**

- [GB200 support with ARM builds](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/release/0.2.0/examples/llm/README.md#build-docker) (Note: currently requires a container build)
- [Planner](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/release/0.2.0/docs/planner.md) - new experimental support for spinning workers up and down based on load
- [Improved K8s deployment workflow](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/release/0.2.0/docs/guides/dynamo_deploy)
  - Installation wizard to enable easy configuration of Dynamo on your Kubernetes cluster
  - CLI to manage your operator-based deployments
  - Consolidate Custom Resources for Dynamo Deployments
  - Documentation improvements (including Minikube guide to installing Dynamo Platform)

**Future plans**

[Dynamo Roadmap](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/762) 

 **Known Issues**
  - Benchmark guides are still being validated on public cloud instances (GCP / AWS)
  - Benchmarks on internal clusters show a 15% degradation from results displayed in summary graphs for multi-node 70B and are being investigated.
   - TensorRT-LLM examples are not working currently in this release - but are being fixed in main.

name: Dynamo Release v0.1.1
body:
Dynamo is an open source project with Apache 2 license. The primary distribution is done via pip wheels with minimal binary size. The ai-dynamo github org hosts 2 repos: dynamo and NIXL. Dynamo is designed as the ideal next generation inference server, building upon the foundations of the Triton Inference Server. While Triton focuses on single-node inference deployments, we are committed to integrating its robust single-node capabilities into Dynamo within the next several months. We will maintain ongoing support for Triton while ensuring a seamless migration path for existing users to Dynamo once feature parity is achieved. As a vendor-agnostic serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple LLM inference engines including TRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang, with varying degrees of maturity and support. 

**Dynamo v0.1.1 features:**

- Benchmarking guides for Single and Multi-Node Disaggregation on H100 (vLLM)
- TensorRT-LLM support for KV Aware Routing
- TensorRT-LLM support for Disaggregation
- ManyLinux and Ubuntu 22.04 Support for wheels and crates
- Unified logging for Python and Rust

**Future plans**

- Instructions for reproducing benchmark guides on GCP and AWS 
- KV Cache Manager as a standalone repository under the ai-dynamo organization. This release will provide functionality for storing and evicting KV cache across multiple memory tiers, including GPU, system memory, local SSD, and object storage.
- Searchable user guides and documentation 
- Multi-node instances for large models
- Initial Planner version supporting dynamic scaling of P / D workers. We will include an early version of the Dynamo Planner, another core component. This initial release will feature heuristic-based dynamic allocation of GPU workers between prefill and decode tasks, as well as model and fleet configuration adjustments based on user traffic patterns. Our vision is to evolve the Planner into a reinforcement learning platform, which will allow users to define objectives and then tune and optimize performance policies automatically based on system feedback.
- vLLM 1.0 support with NIXL and KV Cache Events

 **Known Issues**
  - Benchmark guides are still being validated on public cloud instances (GCP / AWS)
  - Benchmarks on internal clusters show a 15% degradation from results displayed in summary graphs for multi-node 70B and are being investigated.

body:

**Initial Dynamo release features:**

- Disaggregated serving with X prefill and Y decode nodes
- KV aware routing

- Support for K8s deployment 

As a vendor-agnostic serving framework, Dynamo supports multiple LLM inference engines including TRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang at launch, with varying degrees of maturity and support. Our vision is to evolve the Planner into a reinforcement learning platform, which will allow users to define objectives and then tune and optimize performance policies automatically based on system feedback.
Dynamo is designed as the ideal next generation inference server, building upon the foundations of the Triton Inference Server.
